clue.text: Lady into bloomers back in underwear, contrary outfit embraced by different fellow

indicators.note: the letters of the reworked fellow hug the next two pieces between them
a different fellow is the same letters in another order
the back of underwear is its final letter
contrary turns the word for outfit the other way round

parts.note: a rig is an outfit of clothing or kit

explanation.surface: A woman shows off her bloomers under her clothes while a man in odd attire holds her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns FELLOW into FLOWE...L, which embraces R (the back of underwear) and GIR, RIG made 'contrary'. 'Lady into bloomers' is not lingerie: it is a girl keen on flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid child carrying blossoms is a young lady who is, playfully, into blooms.

clue.text: Brains in bum

definitions.meaning: slang for the head or intelligence, as in use your noggin
to bum around is to idle and laze about

explanation.surface: A crude jibe that someone's intelligence is in their backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are slang: the head as seat of intelligence, and the verb for lazing about idly.

clue.text: Skinny female, shivering in the raw outside

indicators.note: the shaken-up letters of in the raw sit outside the letter for female
shivering letters are jumbled and shaken about

explanation.surface: A thin woman trembles with cold, naked out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' rearranges IN THE RAW into WAERTHIN, which goes 'outside' F to give WA-F-ERTHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely thin, like a biscuit, is described as skinny; synonym for very slim.

clue.text: Most unusual to see god in the centre of Chertsey

indicators.note: the god's name goes inside the central letters of the town
the centre of an eight-letter word is its middle two letters

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A rare sighting of a deity in the middle of a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of CHERTSEY is RT; ARES goes 'in' it. Chertsey is a town in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative synonym: the scarcest or least common thing is the most unusual.

clue.text: Single preference, soup slightly off

parts.note: miso is a Japanese soup
gamy meat is high, beginning to go off

explanation.surface: Someone prefers soup that is past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single preference' is not a menu choice: it is preferring to stay single.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hatred of marriage, so a preference for remaining unwed.

clue.text: Devices including wrong and right in European language

indicators.note: the word for devices takes the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: machines are mechanical devices

indicators.note: wrong signals the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Gadgets that hold right and wrong in a continental tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns the first two small pieces into NDAR, which 'including' sets with the next pair of letters just after the opening of the devices word.
explanation.definitionFit: The standard spoken tongue of China is a language, the most widely spoken in the world.

clue.text: Private opening in solid square, cube

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, a square courtyard
a die is a small cube used in games

explanation.surface: A secret opening inside a solid square block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective, but it is the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British term for a soldier of the lowest rank, a private.

clue.text: Squeeze round corners, leaning heads skywards in ravine

indicators.note: in a down entry, going skywards means read from bottom to top
the word for squeeze goes round the two initial letters

parts.note: to hug is to squeeze someone in your arms

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Hugging tightly round bends, heads tilted upward in a canyon.
explanation.walkthrough: HUG goes 'round' C and L (the 'heads' of corners, leaning), making HCLUG, which 'skywards' turns upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a narrow steep-sided gorge, chiefly in the American West.

clue.text: Figure taking off in The Doctor, then want sci-fi film

indicators.note: the reversed number goes inside the medical degree

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: taking off like a plane, the number rises, read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: nine is a figure, a number
to want is to lack

explanation.surface: A dancer leaps inside the doctor's surgery, then a craving for a space movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking off' turns NINE upwards to ENIN, placed 'in' MB. Doctor Who's 'The Doctor' is a false path.
explanation.definitionFit: Title of the 1997 science fiction movie about agents policing aliens on Earth.

clue.text: Rat killer fighting at a distance and at home

parts.note: fighting is war
far means at a distance
in means at home

explanation.surface: A rodent exterminator fights from afar and from indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: This anticoagulant was first developed and used as rodent poison, so a killer of vermin.

clue.text: Hill upsetting me? Not Damon, initially

indicators.note: upsetting knocks the letters over into a new order

parts.note: me is the setter, whose pseudonym is Paul

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of the words

explanation.surface: Racing driver Damon Hill's name is upsetting the speaker, though Damon is not meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the setter, Paul. 'Hill' calls to mind Formula One champion Damon Hill, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Higher ground or elevated country is a hilly area, so a synonym for a hill region.

clue.text: A wake-up call for the Sun?

definitions.text: A wake-up call for the Sun?

parts.words: A wake-up call for the Sun?
parts.note: a common morning greeting to a sleeper, which literally tells the Sun to come up over the horizon and glow

explanation.surface: What you would shout to wake the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the cheery cry used to rouse a sleeper, which also describes what the Sun does at dawn.

clue.text: Home leave always conditional at first, occupying post

indicators.note: occupying puts these letters inside the word for post

parts.note: a station is a post, a place of duty
ay is an old and poetic word for always

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Time off at home is always conditional, at first, on one's posting.
explanation.walkthrough: AY and C go 'occupying' STATION, after its ST. AY (or AYE) meaning ever is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday spent at home rather than travelling is time off, or leave, taken at home.

clue.text: Long throw dismissing opener

indicators.note: dismissing the opener drops the first letter, a cricket image

parts.note: to pitch is to throw

explanation.surface: A long throw dismisses a cricket opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is the verb, as in to long for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn for something is to have an urge or craving for it: synonym as verbs.

clue.text: One little character, after evidence of head lice, considered alone

indicators.note: after places the little character behind the lice evidence

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
nits are the eggs of lice, evidence of infestation
an elf is a small fairy-tale character

explanation.surface: A tiny person, after a lice check, is quarantined alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrase meaning intrinsically, taken by itself without other factors.

clue.text: 8 can be fixed?

parts.note: the answer split as crew inside sable reads men in black, the answer to 8 down, since sable is heraldic black

explanation.surface: Can the answer to 8 be repaired?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay is men (CREW) in black (SABLE), i.e. 8 down. Sable is the heraldic word for black.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be fastened in place with screws can be fixed, as a shelf to a wall.

clue.text: Infant feeding pot with a European coin

indicators.note: the infant feeds into the word for pot, going inside it

parts.note: to pot a ball in snooker is to sink it
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A baby fed from a pot alongside a continental coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is the snooker verb, to sink a ball. This coin is a Bulgarian hundredth of a lev.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor currency unit of Bulgaria, worth one hundredth of a lev: a coin of Europe.

clue.text: City on Polish borders, strangely mesmerising

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are put in an odd order
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A city on the Polish frontier is oddly captivating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' of Polish give PH; 'strangely' mixes them with CITY ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: inducing a trance-like state, as a mesmerist does.

clue.text: Run one!

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an ace is a one on dice or cards

explanation.surface: An order to run a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: run a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest of speed is held by running one, so the clue commands a sprint.

clue.text: Winding course of teeth going the wrong way, right to left

indicators.note: right to left swaps the letter for right for that for left
going the wrong way means the word runs backwards

parts.note: molars are back teeth

explanation.surface: A dental course runs backwards, from right to left.
explanation.walkthrough: MOLARS 'going the wrong way' gives SRALOM; 'right to left' changes its R to L.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski or canoe race zigzagging between gates is a winding course.

clue.text: Married to wife, pain's learnt the hard way — for her lot?

indicators.note: married to attaches the wife's letter to the end of the jumbled words
learning the hard way suggests the letters are knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Wed to his wife, he learnt pain the hard way through her family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hard way' rearranges PAIN'S LEARNT, and W follows. The question mark flags 'her lot' as a definition from the husband's side.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband's wife's family, her mother and father, are his relatives by marriage: her lot.

clue.text: Infiltrating demo, jingoistic icon

indicators.note: infiltrating means the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: An agent infiltrates a jingoistic demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: A small digital picture used in messages is a kind of icon, a symbol on screen.

clue.text: See 1
Reject is into drink

indicators.note: into places is inside the word for drink

parts.note: to down a drink is to drink it

explanation.surface: Turning someone down because they are into drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cast off or refuse to acknowledge, as with a family member.

clue.text: Maintaining cross, return title with bitterness, seeing book's inscription

indicators.note: maintaining means holding the cross inside
return reads the pair of words backwards

parts.note: Sir is a title for a knight
bile is bitterness of temper
X is a cross

explanation.surface: An angry writer reclaims a title bitterly, seeing an inscription.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns SIR + BILE into ELIBRIS, which is 'Maintaining' X.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin 'from the books of': the bookplate or label on a book showing its owner.

clue.text: Picture gives an image, ultimately distorted

indicators.note: distorted letters are bent out of their order
ultimately takes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A painting gives a warped image.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to imagine or visualise it: verb synonyms.

clue.text: Fine stuff not entirely describing English breakfast

indicators.note: describing, in crosswords, means drawing round, so the cloth goes around the letter
not entirely drops the last letter of the fabric

parts.note: muslin is a fine cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Something fine, not quite describing a full English breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims MUSLIN to MUSLI, which goes round E. A 'full English' is a fried breakfast, the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning, an example of breakfast.
